Do you agree with this, or do you think that bringing forth the truth by telling tales is just as important? Give reasons for your response. question 26 A Man Called Ove was Backman’s first book and was a huge hit. Do you think it’s difficult to match the runaway success of the first book for such authors in general? question 27 Fredrick Backman was a blogger and journalist first before he became an author. Do you think having a background in blogging helped Backman develop better plots and characters when he began to write his novel? question 28 Backman is a stay at home dad who feels his time is taken up with his kids and can’t manage to find a routine for his writing. Do you think this kind of lifestyle facilitates your writing or does it make it more difficult? Explain your thoughts. question 29 Backman’s first book is going to be made into a movie though he doesn’t have much of a say in the script. As an author, would you want to take this risk of having someone else adapt your work in a way completely different from what you have envisaged? What kind of risks is the author taking by giving up control of the storyline? question 30 Backman agrees that there is an autobiographical element to every book he writes. Which part of A Man Called Ove do you think is influenced by his real life? question 31 Ove is a grumpy old man who has been grumpy even before his wife died. If you were his neighbor, would you care about such a man, even if he was helpful? question 32 Ove tries many different methods to commit suicide, all of which remain unsuccessful. If you were in his place, which would be your chosen method, if any, of taking your life? question 33 Ove has an inordinate dislike of the men in white shirts who he thinks are out to get him. If Ove himself was working within the system, do you think he would become just like them? question 34 Ove is a grumpy old man, but he begins to thaw a bit when Parwaneh and her daughters come into his life. If you were Ove, what would it take for you to find meaning in life after all the sufferings he has been through? question 35 Ove and Rune were close friends who had a weird way of communicating with each other. If you had a friend like Ove, how would you deal with him? question 36 Ove refused to tell the truth about the theft because he thought that would be ‘telling tales.' If you were in Ove’s shoes, would you have felt comfortable pinpointing the thief and bringing him to justice or not? Why? question 37 Ove offers shelter, albeit reluctantly, to the homosexual boy whose father threw him out of the house. If you were Ove with that kind of worldview, how would you have dealt with the situation? question 38 Ove refuses to update his knowledge of the ways of the world, including technology. If you were Ove, how would you deal with an ever-changing world that has left you behind? Quiz Questions question 50 Backman is from _______. Quiz Answers True Saab False: Ove disliked the bureaucracy, thinking the people who worked for the system did their best to run roughshod over the helpless people in their power. True Parking Clown Drive First Journalism Blogging False: Backman is a stay at home dad and just snatches time from his hectic life to write. He prefers it this way.
